notes: Round 4 closes review-3 findings. MAJOR 1: invalid_params/malformed_frame/unsupported_frame_type are no longer terminal (the gateway raises invalid_params for contract violations that fail every message); terminal now needs per-payload evidence (payload_too_large from local encodeFrame, content-size text) AND non-uniformity - candidates are held without advancing the cursor and only commit when a later message lands, with a bail-out at RECOVERY_UNIFORM_FAILURE_LIMIT consecutive candidates. MAJOR 2: channel.messages.fetch is guarded per conversation (failed + fetchError), each channel's replay runs in its own try/catch, and only a fully clean pass resets the backoff - every other exit arms the scheduled retry. MINOR 3: a never-evicted per-conversation dead-letter digest (count, first/last id and timestamps) keeps mass discards auditable past the 50-record cap. MINOR 4: a bounded, persisted cross-pass attempt ledger converges on the discard threshold for alternating terminal/transient failures. MINOR 5: dead-letter recording is idempotent per message id. NIT 6: quarantine and ledger retention sort on explicit persisted seq metadata instead of JS key order. Durability: the cursor/dead-letter save fsyncs the temp file before the atomic rename and best-effort fsyncs the directory, with the residual window documented. Recovery still does not backfill threads/DMs (needs Discord thread enumeration, out of scope); their watermarks are retained under the quarantine cap. Each new test was verified to fail under a targeted source mutation. The full package run emits an expected session-rebind startup-failure diagnostic from its existing test scenario; the suite completed with zero failing tests.
